name: Push firmware to a device
description: One command that publishes a build (optional), pushes it to ONE named device, waits for the device's result and prints the process. Zero dependencies, runs on the device-development machine with Node 18+, reuses the existing publish token and endpoints. The device firmware needs no changes.
description_zh: 一条命令 = 发布（可选）+ 下发给一台指定设备 + 等结果 + 打印过程。零依赖、Node 18+ 直接跑，复用现有发布 token 与端点，设备端无需任何改动。

requires.token: Bearer — the publish token (master or a wk_ work token); needed for push and --cancel, not for --list/--status
requires.config: publish.config.json (server + token + project.id + optional buildDir/assets), or --config <path>; --server overrides the server URL
requires.network: plain HTTP works (self-signed HTTPS would need NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS=<crt>)

to.note: exactly one device; accepts 34:85:a1:b2:c3:d4 / '34 85 A1 B2 C3 D4' / 3485a1b2c3d4, normalised to 12 lowercase hex

build.note: --build [dir] — publish first (dir optional, defaults to config buildDir); snapshot by default

release.note: --release <id> — push a version already on the server (snapshot or release)

latest.note: --latest — the latest release for the device's chip family; needs --project when several projects share that variant

project.note: limit --latest (and the chip-family lookup) to one project id

force.note: supersede an unresolved command for a DIFFERENT release (same release = re-entry, handled automatically)

forceChip.note: allow a chip-family mismatch (default: refuse; pushing the wrong chip can brick a device)

allowUnknown.note: skip the local 'device must exist in GET /api/devices' gate and let the server decide (a device that never reported cannot be online, so expect exit 9)

skipIfSame.note: --no-skip-if-same forces a re-flash when the device is already on the target release

promote.note: --build produces a snapshot; --promote changes its type to 'release' (and attaches the note). `variant.latest` already points at it from the moment it was published — promote does NOT move latest

status.note: read-only recheck: prints the state and the full process chain, zero side effects; exit code matches what --wait would have concluded (5 = still unresolved)

cancel.note: cancel the device's unresolved command (the server's `unresolved` field decides which one, not `lastCommand`)

list.note: print the device list and exit; add --to to show one device

json.note: machine-readable output on stdout (human lines move to stderr); contract in /docs/PUSH-TO-DEVICE.md §2.4

dryRun.note: print what WOULD happen, make zero requests (gates are therefore not evaluated and it says so)

params.noOfflineOverride: a device that is offline at dispatch time is cancelled server-side; there is deliberately no flag to queue it

exit_codes.1: device reported failed (the device's own detail is printed)
exit_codes.4: target unknown: device never reported, or release/candidate missing
exit_codes.5: timeout waiting for a result (or: --status found the command still unresolved)
exit_codes.8: skipped (not a failure): device already on the target release
exit_codes.9: the command was NOT delivered: device offline at dispatch time (412 + cancelled record). The same code is used when a command is cancelled while waiting — the message says which
exit_codes.10: the device has an unresolved command for a DIFFERENT release (use --force to supersede); also reported when the waited command ends up superseded
exit_codes.11: cancelled a DELIVERED command: too late to stop the device, but redelivery stopped
exit_codes.12: nothing to cancel (no unresolved command, or it had already finished)
exit_codes.130: interrupted (Ctrl+C) while waiting: the command keeps running on the server; use --status to recheck

gates: the target device must exist in GET /api/devices (else exit 4) — the server auto-creates entries for unknown deviceIds, so a typo used to queue silently
release.chipFamily must equal device.chip (else exit 7; 'cannot verify' counts as a mismatch)
the device must be online at the instant of dispatch — enforced by the SERVER, which answers 412 and keeps a cancelled record (exit 9); the CLI checks the same gate up front to fail fast
an unresolved command for the SAME releaseId = re-entry: adopt that command and keep waiting (not an error, no re-dispatch)
an unresolved command for a DIFFERENT releaseId = 409 -> exit 10 unless --force

apis.list_devices: GET /api/devices (public) — target lookup, chip/firmware/online, and the unresolved command
apis.get_command: GET /api/devices/{deviceId}/commands/{commandId} (public) — exact by-id polling while waiting
apis.dispatch: POST /api/devices/{deviceId}/commands (Bearer) — 412 when the device is offline, 409 when a command is already unresolved

process_visibility.what_is_printed: each new stage as it happens (device pickup, per-phase progress with percent, receipt) plus a final verdict line with the total time
process_visibility.on_failure_or_timeout: the FULL chain is printed, including a relative time per step, where exactly it stopped (pending / delivered) and how long it has been stuck, plus the hint for --status
process_visibility.no_fake_progress: if the device never reports progress the CLI says so explicitly instead of inventing a percentage
process_visibility.stuck_rules: pending > 30s => warn; delivered with no progress report > 120s => warn; progress older than 60s while unresolved => warn

json_output: see /docs/PUSH-TO-DEVICE.md §2.4 — { ok, skipped, published, device, command, elapsedMs, exitCode, error }

related_tools.ota_console: /ota.json — the same operation by hand in a browser (page dispatch is refused identically when the device is offline)
related_tools.device_sim: /tools/device-sim/index.js — fake ESP32 for testing the whole loop without hardware

not_implemented: watch-style auto-push (the existing `publish --watch` only publishes; it does not push)
